known_issues: win32-input-mode is not implemented. Programs that read Windows key records instead of bytes (PowerShell's line editor, anything on crossterm such as Codex) therefore see legacy Shift+Enter as Alt+Enter and cannot tell Ctrl+Shift+letter from Ctrl+letter. Measured: switching the mode on would fix that for them and at the same time hand every byte-reading program that has not asked for the kitty protocol a plain CR for Shift+Enter. No per-key trick avoids the trade; it needs to be a setting or a per-program decision.

Whether Claude Code asks PROTEUS for the kitty protocol was not observed (running it would touch ~/.claude and the person's usage). If it does, it gets CSI 13;2u; if it does not, it gets ESC CR as before. Both paths are tested, the choice between them is the program's.
Real key events from a window were not exercised in this run (no window may be opened). The event's fields are tested; the last inch, the window library filling those fields on this keyboard, is not.

Caps Lock and Num Lock are never reported as modifiers in the kitty protocol (kitty and foot report them on non-text keys; Alacritty does not). Deliberate: a program comparing the modifier field exactly would lose Shift+Enter whenever Num Lock is on.
alacritty_terminal reads SGR 21 as 'bold off' (the Linux console's reading). ECMA-48, xterm and kitty define it as double underline. SGR 4:2 works.

alacritty_terminal has no grapheme clustering: an emoji with a skin tone takes 4 cells, a ZWJ family 6, a heart with its emoji selector 1. Text after them sits in different columns from where a cluster-aware program expects it.

alacritty_terminal forgets keyboard flags set in place (CSI = flags u) when the screen is switched, because it restores from its stack; and inside a synchronized update the flags query can be answered with the flags from before the update.
xterm's modifyOtherKeys (CSI > 4 ; n m) is ignored: alacritty_terminal 0.25 does not track it. Programs that use it instead of the kitty protocol get legacy keys.
Colour emoji still render in one colour, flags as two letters, skin tone modifiers as a swatch. No ligatures.
Combining marks are overlaid, not shaped: the font's own mark anchors are not applied, so a mark over a capital or a wide letter can sit slightly off.
Hyperlinks (OSC 8) are stored per cell but not shown or clickable. Blink (SGR 5, 6) and overline (SGR 53) never reach PROTEUS: the terminal library drops them.
In the alternate screen the mouse wheel still sends SS3 arrows under cursor-key mode even when the program has kitty flags on (the protocol says CSI); programs accept both.
The undercurl's height (1.25 x underline thickness, at least 1.5 px) and the dot and dash sizes were chosen by looking at PNGs at 10 and 15 point; nobody has judged them in a window.

forge/samples/draw.vt, like basic.vt, is stored by git with LF and checked out with CRLF (core.autocrlf); on a checkout without that setting its lines would not return to column 1. conformance.vt places everything by address and is stored byte for byte.

From review. A key held down while the window gains focus is typed into the session: the window library synthesizes a press for every key that is down at that moment and app.rs does not look at is_synthetic. So Enter still held from launching the window runs an empty line. This was so before this lane. Not fixed here: the change is one line in app.rs (ignore synthetic presses, keep synthetic releases) but it cannot be tested without a window.

From review. The release of Enter, Tab or Backspace held with a modifier is not reported unless the program asked for every key. That is the specification's sentence read literally; kitty's source reports those (Shift+Enter down CSI 13;2u, up CSI 13;2:3u; read from kitty/key_encoding.c, kitty was not run). A program tracking held keys sees Shift+Enter go down and never come up.
From review. alacritty_terminal also forgets flags set in place (CSI = flags u) on a pop, not only on a screen switch: set 5, push 3, pop leaves 0 where kitty leaves 5.
From review. Ctrl+Shift+Delete changes only this window's parser. It is not in the journal, so a window that picks the session up again replays the program's push and has the flags on again.

From review. Alt with a key that types a non-Latin letter sends ESC and that letter (Alt+с sends ESC с); kitty sends ESC and the Latin key in that position. Left as it was: both are defensible and no program was seen to depend on it.
From review. A dead key followed by Enter or Backspace drops the accent: the text Windows reports then contains a control character and is discarded whole.

From review. Function key F3 with a modifier is CSI 1;m R in legacy mode, as in xterm and as before this lane. kitty uses CSI 13;m ~ because the xterm form has the shape of a cursor position report; under the protocol PROTEUS uses kitty's form.

From review. The key fixes found in review rest on reading the window library's source (winit 0.30.13, platform_impl/windows/keyboard.rs) and one measurement of this machine's US layout. No key was pressed in a window, and no non-US layout was installed to check AltGr, dead keys or Cyrillic.

From review. conformance.vt is stored byte for byte only because git takes it for a binary file (it holds a lone CR). A .gitattributes line (forge/samples/conformance.vt -text) would make that deliberate; not added here because .gitattributes is shared by every lane.

user_notes: Nothing changes for a program that asks for nothing: Shift+Enter is still ESC CR. A program that asks for the kitty protocol now gets real Shift+Enter (CSI 13;2u), Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+Shift chords and, if it asks, key releases.

To see what any key sends, run `proteus keys` in a shell inside the terminal (`proteus keys --flags 1` to see it as an agent interface would, `proteus keys --records` to see it as PowerShell does). Ctrl+C twice ends it.
In PowerShell's own prompt Shift+Enter still arrives as Alt+Enter, as before. Fixing that is the win32-input-mode decision above.

New: the terminal now answers 'do you support the kitty keyboard protocol', so programs that ask (Neovim, fish over ssh, some agent interfaces) will switch it on. If one of them dies without switching it off and Ctrl+C starts printing [99;5u at the prompt, press Ctrl+Shift+Delete.
